# @231self/opencode-compaction

Context management for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and Kilo sessions:
the deterministic context optimiser, a priced "should I compact now?"
advisory, and the plumbing to compact on request. Install it alongside
[`@231self/opencode-router`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@231self/opencode-router):

```sh
opencode plugin add @231self/opencode-compaction
```

## Why this exists

An agent session's context is sent again on every turn. Providers bill most
of it as cache reads (cheap), so letting context grow feels free — until the
session nears its window and someone summarizes the history. Summarizing
destroys the prompt cache: the next turn re-writes the compacted prefix at
the cache-write price instead of reading the old one at the cache-read
price. Whether compaction pays is arithmetic, and this plugin does the
arithmetic for you before anything is thrown away.

It also knows when *not* to summarize. Compacting in the middle of a
derivation discards partial work — the failure mode the SelfCompact paper
measured. And for review steps, a fresh subagent with no context often
judges work better than a session drowning in it (the Elephant-Goldfish
pattern). The advisory weighs all three: keep, compact, or delegate.

## What you get

**The optimiser.** When a turn's request does not fit the model's budget,
oversized tool outputs are deduplicated, truncated, and stubbed in a fixed
order until it fits. Recent turns, system instructions, and error outputs
are never touched. If nothing can make it fit, the session is left alone and
the host is told to compact. When the request fits, nothing is changed.

**The advisory.** Each turn computes a verdict and stores it with the
session:

- `compact-now` — a sub-task just finished, the context is under pressure,
  and compaction pays for itself within the expected horizon.
- `delegate` — the next step looks like review or verification. Send it to a
  fresh subagent instead.
- `not-yet` — keep working.

The verdict combines three layers: deterministic signals from the message
shape (a tool burst followed by a summary is a sub-task boundary), the
cache economics (break-even turns, per-turn savings), and — only when the
signals are unclear — a small local judge answering a rubric. The verdict
cannot flicker: changes wait out a cooldown that grows with the judge's
measured instability.

The cache hit rate is the share the provider served from cache over the last
five steps on the current model, or the router's turn log after a plugin
restart. An idle gap longer than the provider's cache lifetime is treated as a
cold cache. `/ctx` shows the rate, its source, and the sample
count; the configured `pin.cacheHitRatio` is only the fallback before the
first measurement.

The decision horizon stays `expectedTurns`, but `/ctx` also shows the same
economics at 3, 8, and 15 turns (`horizons`), so you can see where the answer
flips instead of guessing when the session ends.

Context size comes from the prompt the provider billed — `input +
cache.read + cache.write` on the newest request — whenever a request has run
since the last compaction. Counting messages measures parts the host prunes
from the request, so the message estimate is only the fallback, and `/ctx`
says which one it is showing.

Cost economics need real prices, and not every model publishes them. `/ctx`
keeps the cases apart instead of printing the same numbers for all of them.
A model with its own prices computes break-even turns and per-turn savings.
A flat-rate pool publishes zeros for a model whose list price lives in a
sibling catalog entry — `xiaomi-token-plan-sgp/mimo-v2.6-pro` and
`xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` are the same model — so the comparison is computed at
that list price and labelled `priced at list price · xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`,
alongside the plan fact that it costs you nothing either way. A `-free` model
with no priced sibling, and a model with no catalog entry at all, are shown as
`no reference price` and `no price data`. A break-even is never stated as your
own cost when it was not computed from your own prices.

Because a plan makes cost irrelevant but the window finite, `/ctx` reports
capacity next to the size: the model's limit, the headroom left, and the share
free. When headroom drops below 15% the closing note says so rather than
telling you to keep working.

**`/ctx here`** asks the host to compact this session; the host runs an
admitted compaction at the next step boundary. `/ctx` reports what it did with
the request (`last /ctx here`, `outcome accepted` or `failed · http 409`), and
only a status code or an error name is ever persisted — an error message may
echo prompt text. The request never repeats on its own.

The compacted size and the one-time cost are calibrated from real compactions.
After a compaction the plugin observed as it happened, it compares its
prediction with the size that actually followed and keeps the rolling error. A
checkpoint first noticed after a restart is old history and records no
prediction: using the context as it stands now as the "post-compaction" size
produced a 2,352% phantom error on a session that had grown for two days.
The first post-compaction turn's reported reads, writes, and misses replace the
modelled rebuild cost. The summary request is measured from the completed checkpoint's
own token usage and model when OpenCode supplies them; otherwise its cost is
estimated from the context it had to read and the summary it produced.

**`/ctx`** in the TUI opens with the current context size and growth, then the
verdict with its numbers and what to do about it. **`/ctx here`** asks the
host to compact this session; the
request clears itself even if the host refuses. OpenCode already has its own
`/compact`; this plugin leaves that command alone and does not register a
`compact` alias.

## Settings

In `~/.config/omlx-router/config.json`:

```json
{
  "compaction": {
    "enabled": true,
    "expectedTurns": 8,
    "baseCooldown": 3,
    "judgeRefine": true,
    "summaryTokens": 1200,
    "horizons": [3, 8, 15],
    "cacheWindow": 5
  }
}
```

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` turns the advisory off. |
| `expectedTurns` | `8` | Decision horizon for "does compaction pay?" |
| `baseCooldown` | `3` | Turns a verdict change must wait. |
| `judgeRefine` | `true` | Let the judge resolve unclear cases. |
| `summaryTokens` | `1200` | Assumed size of a compaction summary. |
| `horizons` | `[3, 8, 15]` | Turns shown in the `/ctx` projection table. |
| `cacheWindow` | `5` | Provider steps used for the measured hit rate. |
| `cacheTtlMs` | `0` | Global cache lifetime override; `0` uses the provider table. |
| `cacheTtlByProvider` | Anthropic/OpenAI 5 min | Per-provider idle expiry; `0` disables it. |

The file is read as strict JSON, so keep comments out of it.

## Calibration

The judge's compaction verdicts are not perfectly stable. Measure how much
they move and the advisory's cooldown will respect it:

```sh
bun run compaction:calibrate --repeat 3
```

This writes `~/.local/state/omlx-router/compaction-noise.json`. It needs the
local judge running (the same oMLX endpoint the router uses).

Real compactions update `~/.local/state/omlx-router/compaction-calibration.json`
on their own. It stores the rolling summary size, the summary request's token
buckets, the first post-compaction turn's buckets, and the error of the last
size prediction per model. Delete it to return to the configured assumptions.

```sh
bun run compaction:report
```

That is a checkout command, not part of the installed package. It prints the
measured summary size, the last predicted-versus-actual size, the mean absolute
relative error, the rebuild buckets, and the sample counts per model. If the
prediction error stays large, the summary estimate is not earning its place
yet. The means are exponential after 20 samples, not a full sliding window.

The cache-lifetime defaults for Anthropic and OpenAI are configurable
assumptions about those providers, not guarantees. Unknown providers do not
expire by time. The calibration stream is the OpenCode V2 event API; the Kilo
transform path has no equivalent measurement and uses the fallbacks. If
another process holds the calibration lock, the update is skipped and the
advisory still runs; a crashed writer's `.lock` file needs manual removal.

Two other research tools:

```sh
bun run compaction:ablation --repeat 3              # fixed vs signal vs hybrid, on fixtures
bun run tolerance:eval --repeat 2 --model my-model  # per-model degradation under compaction
```

The ablation is offline by default; add `--judge` to use the live oMLX judge.
The signal and hybrid arms run the shipped advisory, including the economics
veto and the cooldown. Repeats are real samples. The tolerance bench scores
each model with its full context and with a compacted checkpoint; a
deliberately lossy control task is reported separately so a model is not
punished for refusing to answer from missing evidence.

## Current limits

The cache hit rate is measured from provider-reported usage. The compacted
size is calibrated from observed checkpoints, and the rebuild cost comes from
the first post-compaction turn when the host reports it. When OpenCode includes
the compaction request's own tokens on the checkpoint, that is used; otherwise
the summary cost is estimated. Native and automatic compactions are calibrated
the same way, because the checkpoint carries the fields. `/ctx` labels each
number `measured`, `estimated`, `turn log`, or `modelled` so the difference
stays visible.

## Privacy

The advisory works on signals: token counts, message roles, tool names,
growth. Decision state stores numbers and booleans. The judge call is the
one place prompt text is used, and it is never written to logs or state.

## Development

```sh
bun test packages/compaction/tests    # offline suite (judge mocked)
bun run test:rust                     # the optimise core
```

Part of the [opencode-router](https://github.com/231self/opencode-router)
monorepo. Apache-2.0.

# Changelog

## 0.1.6 — 2026-11-23

### Added

- Flat-rate plans get real economics instead of a dead end. A plan pool
  publishes zeros for a model whose list price is in a sibling catalog entry,
  and 0.1.5 answered `worth it no` for it — which made compaction look
  pointless on a plan. `/ctx` now computes the comparison at that list price
  and says so: `priced at list price · xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`, `break-even 1
  turn (at list price)`, `worth it yes · free on your plan`. A `-free` model
  with no priced sibling is still shown as `no reference price · $0 marginal`.
- Capacity in the `context` section: size against the model's limit, headroom
  and percent free. A plan makes cost irrelevant but the window finite, so
  when headroom drops below 15% the closing note says the window is nearly
  full rather than "keep working".
- `/ctx` reports what the host did with the last `/ctx here` request
  (`last /ctx here`, `outcome accepted` or `failed · http 409`).

### Fixed

- `/ctx here` no longer fails silently. The request path swallowed every error
  and skipped the host call without comment when `session.compact` was absent,
  so it could look broken forever with no way to tell which happened. The
  outcome is now recorded and shown; only a status code or an error name is
  persisted, never an error message, which may echo prompt text.
- A `/ctx here` request is also honored at `session.step.ended`, the step
  boundary where the host says an admitted compaction runs, instead of only
  from inside an in-flight request.
- A projection at a sibling's list price never vetoes a structural
  `compact-now`. The veto now applies only to the user's own prices: a
  projection must not block an action whose real marginal cost is zero.
- `1 turn` instead of `1 turns`; no nested parentheses in `summary cost`.
- Depends on `@231self/opencode-shared` `^0.1.4`.

## 0.1.5 — 2026-11-23

### Fixed

- The report no longer prints economics it did not compute. A model with no
  usable prices produced `per turn $0.0000`, `break-even never turns`,
  `worth it no` and `summary cost $0.0000 (estimated)` — placeholders that
  read as results — and silently dropped the `horizons` section. The report
  now distinguishes a flat-rate plan (`flat plan · $0 marginal`, no cost
  savings) from missing data (`no price data · not computed`, `worth it
  unknown`), and always renders the horizons, saying why a row has no number.
- The context size comes from the prompt the provider billed
  (`input + cache.read + cache.write` of the newest request) whenever a
  request has run since the last compaction, and from the message estimate
  otherwise. `/ctx` shows which. A request's billed prefill is the only
  authoritative size; counting messages measures parts the host prunes.
- A prediction is recorded only for a compaction observed as it happens. A
  checkpoint first noticed after a restart or an install used the context as
  it stands now as the "post-compaction" size, which is how a session that had
  grown for two days recorded a 2,352% phantom prediction error. The summary
  size is still learned either way.
- Predicted and actual compacted sizes are on one scale, so a prediction error
  now measures the compacted-size model rather than a unit mismatch.

### Changed

- `/ctx` opens with a `context` section: current size, growth, and the source
  (`billed` or `estimated`).
- `summary cost` and `rebuild` say `modelled` when they are modelled from
  prices. They claimed `estimated` and `modelled` respectively for the same
  situation.
- Depends on `@231self/opencode-shared` `^0.1.3`.

## 0.1.4 — 2026-11-23

### Fixed

- Depend on `@231self/opencode-shared` `^0.1.2`. Version 0.1.3 imported the
  new `contextMessageTokens` export but declared `^0.1.1`, so npm could
  resolve shared 0.1.1, which lacks it, and the plugin failed to load. The
  code is otherwise identical to 0.1.3.

## 0.1.3 — 2026-11-23

### Fixed

- The context hook measures the active session (`ctx.session.context`) instead
  of its local outgoing message segment. In a 233k-token session the plugin
  recorded 7,461 tokens, so `/ctx` reported `not-yet` from the small-context
  branch while the session was under real pressure. The active size now drives
  `lastContextTokens`, growth, checkpoint detection, and the compacted tail.
  `contextMessageTokens` is shared by the active-context counter and the tail
  estimator.

## 0.1.2 — 2026-11-22

### Added

- The advisory prices with the cache hit rate the provider actually reported
  over the last five steps on the current model (`cacheWindow`). An idle gap
  longer than the provider's cache lifetime is treated as a cold cache; the
  defaults are five minutes for Anthropic and OpenAI, and no expiry for
  unknown providers. `pin.cacheHitRatio` remains the fallback until the first
  measurement. `/ctx` shows the rate, source, and sample count.
- `/ctx` shows the same economics at 3, 8, and 15 turns (`horizons`), not just
  at the decision horizon.
- Real compactions calibrate the estimate. The post-compaction context size
  replaces the assumed summary size; the first post-compaction turn's reported
  usage replaces the modelled rebuild cost; the summary request is read from
  the completed checkpoint's own token usage and model when OpenCode supplies
  them, and estimated otherwise. Observations are stored per
  model in `compaction-calibration.json`, and `/ctx` labels each number
  measured, estimated, or modelled.
- Each compaction also records the size the plugin predicted against the size
  the host actually sent. `/ctx` shows the last prediction and the mean
  absolute relative error; `bun run compaction:report` prints the same
  calibration for every model without a live session.

### Fixed

- The summary request's cost now comes from the completed checkpoint's own
  `tokens` and `model`, which OpenCode supplies for manual, automatic, and
  native compactions. Timestamp-based attribution of ordinary model steps is
  gone, so a slow turn can no longer be billed as compaction.
- A compaction checkpoint's summary is counted in the prefill by both the
  fallback token counter and the optimiser, so the compacted size and the
  predicted size use the same definition.
- Rebuild capture pairs by assistant-message id and start time, ignores steps
  that started before the checkpoint, and records the model that actually ran
  the step.
- A delayed advisory re-reads the pin before writing, abandons the write if the
  pin was deleted, and preserves a newer same-model variant, force flag,
  redirect, request marker, or advisory. Overflow compares redirects
  structurally and writes the cleared state in one update.
- Calibration updates take a cross-process lock that fails fast instead of
  stealing another writer's lock. A failed commit does not advance the pin's
  checkpoint, arm rebuild capture, or consume a rebuild sample.
- Checkpoint deduplication lives inside the locked update and in the
  calibration artifact rather than the routing pin, and observation writes
  preserve that metadata.
- The prediction compared at the next compaction is the one stored by the last
  advisory for the same model; opaque or empty checkpoints are counted but
  not used to learn a size or an error.
- Prices are resolved per token count (`tierAt`), including strict `gt`
  thresholds and partial overrides. Measured summary and rebuild samples are
  priced at each observation's own prefill and averaged as dollars, not at the
  mean prefill. An explicit zero cache-write price is no longer replaced.
- Cache samples ignore zero-prefill steps and mixed-model turn-log seeds before
  choosing between live and persisted data, and the window is bounded by the
  live ring.
- The economics veto runs after the guard, so a held `compact-now` cannot
  survive an unprofitable estimate. Horizons use net payback for `worth it`.
- The usage stream's debug path logs a fixed message instead of stringifying
  an exception that may carry prompt text.
- The `/ctx` popup test enforces 72 columns, and an unknown command is clipped
  before it reaches the popup.

## 0.1.1 — 2026-11-22

### Fixed

- The TUI command is `/ctx` only. OpenCode already owns `/compact`, so the
  plugin's slash command — and its `ctx` alias — duplicated or shadowed the
  native command. `/ctx` shows the advisory; `/ctx here` asks the host to
  compact. The popup copy now says what will happen instead of describing the
  hook machinery.

## 0.1.0 — 2026-11-22

### Added

- Initial release. The context optimiser moves out of `@231self/opencode-router`
  (which becomes pure model selection): the `optimise` WASM core with its
  explicit ABI (`alloc`, `dealloc`, `optimise`, `result_len`, `abi_version`),
  the request builder and in-place plan application, the V2 `context` hook
  (optimise + pin measurement), and the Kilo
  `experimental.chat.messages.transform` path.
- The compaction advisory. Each turn produces one of `compact-now`, `delegate`,
  or `not-yet` from three layers: deterministic trajectory signals (a tool
  burst followed by synthesis is a sub-task boundary), the cache economics
  from `@231self/opencode-shared` (break-even turns and a veto when compaction
  does not pay within the horizon), and a small local judge that refines only
  uncertain candidates. A failed judge call leaves the deterministic verdict
  standing.
- Anti-oscillation: a verdict change waits out a cooldown that grows with the
  judge's measured instability, stored by
  `bun run compaction:calibrate --repeat n` in
  `~/.local/state/omlx-router/compaction-noise.json`.
- `/compact` (alias `/ctx`) shows the current verdict with its numbers, and
  `/compact here` asks the host to compact the session; the request clears
  itself even if the host refuses.
